_meta.welcomeMessage:
Welcome to Kiro CLI Guide!

Your friendly AI sidekick, ready to help you get the most out of the CLI. Here's what I can help with:

- Slash commands — /agent, /context, /tools and more
- Built-in tools — read, code, grep... basically superpowers
- Configuration settings — tweak things to your heart's content
- Features — MCP, Code Intelligence, and everything in between
- Create and modify agents, prompts, and configs in ~/.kiro/ and .kiro/

Go ahead, ask me anything about Kiro CLI — no question too weird!

Some fan favorites:
- "How do I save a conversation?"
- "What tools are available?"
- "How does the code tool work?"
- "Create a new agent for me"

Tip: Type /guide again to return to your previous agent

skills.name: adopt-project
skills.description: "Bring the grey-matter workflow into a repo that already has code and history: characterize the as-is model from the code, reconcile around what exists, seed a triaged board, and wire the plumbing — ending in a fully adopted repo. Use to adopt/onboard an existing (brownfield) project. Trigger: adopt this project, onboard existing repo, bring grey-matter into this codebase, brownfield adoption."

skills.name: changelog
skills.description: "Maintain CHANGELOG.md in Keep a Changelog format with user-facing entries. Use when recording what changed for a release, updating the Unreleased section, or asked to write/update the changelog."

skills.name: cheat-sheet
skills.description: "List every skill in this set by category with a one-line description. Use when the user wants a quick reference card of available skills, asks \"what skills are there\", or \"list all commands\"."

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: "Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and files findings as tickets. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\"."

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

skills.name: compass
skills.description: Find which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo. Use when you (or the agent) are unsure which skill to reach for, want to see how the skills fit together, or ask "what should I use for X".

skills.name: conformance-audit
skills.description: "Audit a repo's skills, tool scripts, agent guidance, and docs against grey-matter's current standards, then apply the mechanically-safe fixes behind an approval gate. Use to re-conform an adopted repo as guidance evolves, or as a step inside adopt-project. Trigger: conformance audit, check repo against standards, re-conform, does this repo still follow current conventions."

skills.name: curate-docs
skills.description: "Review docs/agents and .scratch for promotion and deletion: graduate mature notes into skills, move reference docs into a skill's references, and prune stale or superseded material."

skills.name: delivery-dashboard
skills.description: "Maintain one evolving HTML dashboard showing what delivered work lets people do. Use when updating a delivery dashboard, showing shipped versus planned experiences, or presenting progress visually after work worth surfacing."

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model (app/backend/business software). Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording an ADR. For a game's real-time systems and design model, use game-modeling instead.

skills.name: foreign
skills.description: Isolated foreign sentinel.

skills.name: game-modeling
skills.description: Build and sharpen a game's design model, mechanics, systems, and the core loop. Use when discussing game mechanics or terminology, writing a mechanics glossary, or recording a design decision. For a game's backend/economy/meta (business software), use domain-modeling instead.

skills.name: game-native-design
skills.description: "Build games that feel like games, not web apps. Use when designing or reviewing game code: the loop, simulation state, performance, feel, or when another skill needs the game-native vocabulary. Reach for the matching engine appendix once the engine is known."

skills.name: grill-me
skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

skills.name: grill-with-docs
skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design that also leaves a paper trail (glossary and decision records). Use when grilling inside a working directory.

skills.name: grilling
skills.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

skills.name: handoff
skills.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

skills.name: implement
skills.description: "Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets."

skills.name: implement-spec
skills.description: "Implement the result of to-spec and to-tickets in code, a whole spec on one integration branch."

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, classify each by regime, present them as a full-bodied visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

skills.name: init-project
skills.description: "Set up a new project's agent conventions once: AGENTS.md, scratch dir, gitignore, tkt, and whatever else the installed skills need tracked. Use when the user asks to initialize a repo for this workflow, or when adopt-project needs the missing plumbing created."

skills.name: line-craft
skills.description: Line craft for fiction prose and dialogue — feeling written as acts and errands, then the lines checked against a catalog of sentimental shapes. Use when drafting or revising story prose or dialogue, when the author rejects a line as sentimental, portentous or "emo", or when setting up a project's prose shape check.

skills.name: orient
skills.description: "Session-start pickup: get on the frontier and start the top ticket. Reads the board, resumes a live thread or claims the top ready ticket, and only pauses for something genuinely pressing. Use when starting or resuming a session, or asking 'where were we / what's next / pick up where we left off'."

skills.name: pr
skills.description: "Use when writing a PR body."

skills.name: prototype
skills.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, explore what a UI should look like, or find whether a game mechanic is fun.

skills.name: readme
skills.description: "Keep README.md honest and current: what the project is, how to install and use it, its status. Use at release time or when the README has drifted from reality."

skills.name: reconcile-tickets
skills.description: "End-of-session ticket pass: make every open ticket current, capture all untracked work as tickets, and set ordering so the frontier surfaces the right next picks. Use when wrapping up a session, auditing ticket health, or asking 'is everything captured?'."

skills.name: release
skills.description: "Prepare, verify, stage, publish or resume a coordinated versioned release with GitHub and plugin artifacts."

skills.name: research
skills.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a cited Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

skills.name: research-audit
skills.description: Validate and score a research findings file against its sources. Use after research produces a findings file, or when the user wants a cited analysis checked for citation accuracy, source trust, and currency.

skills.name: retro
skills.description: "Conduct a retrospective on a coding session: read it from a fresh context and propose environment fixes (checks, guardrails, steering), classified mechanical vs judgement. Use when a session ends, after a build that went sideways, or when wrap-session reaches its retro step."

skills.name: review-skill
skills.description: Review one upstream skill for adaptation into grey-matter. Use when deciding whether to keep, adapt, drop, or replace a mattpocock/skills skill, one at a time.

skills.name: spike-options
skills.description: "Compare competing approaches with throwaway builds, then agree an integration plan. Use when a hard-to-reverse choice is cheap to spike and uncertainty needs observation rather than more reasoning: compare alternatives, spike options, test competing designs."

skills.name: sync
skills.description: "Pull grey-matter current and re-synchronize the coupled pieces — deployed skills, the tkt command surface, ticket IDs, and repo invariants — then redeploy. Use when updating this repo and pushing the skills back out to the harnesses, or asking to 'pull and deploy' / 'sync and redeploy'."

skills.name: tdd
skills.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

skills.name: teach
skills.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

skills.name: tkt-core
skills.description: "Track tasks as markdown files in your git repo. Use when managing tickets, checking the frontier (what's ready), claiming work, closing tasks, creating tickets, decomposing work into a task graph, or validating project health. Trigger: tkt, tickets, what to work on, create ticket, validate tickets, decompose, break into tasks, work breakdown, task graph, ticket format, blocked by, backlog, park this, defer."

skills.name: tkt-orient
skills.description: "Start-of-session pickup from the reconciled plan and tickets: read the frontier, in-progress threads, and plan ordering that tkt-reconcile left behind, flag stale WIP, and propose the next step. Use when starting a session, resuming after a break, or asking 'where were we?' / 'what's next?' / 'pick up where we left off'. Trigger: start of session, orient, resume, pick up where we left off, where were we, what's next, catch me up, continue, session start, what's on the board."

skills.name: tkt-reconcile
skills.description: "End-of-session ticket + plan pass: make every ticket current, capture all open work as tickets, and re-prioritize/re-sequence the plan to match current priorities and work streams. Use when wrapping up a session, auditing ticket health, after planning, when work feels untracked, or asking 'is everything captured?' / 'update the plan'. Trigger: sync tickets, update the plan, re-prioritize, end of session ticket pass, ticket review, are tickets current, is everything tracked, ticket audit, ticket hygiene, wrap up tickets, tag scope, work stream."

skills.name: tkt-work
skills.description: "Claim and execute a ticket from the frontier: pick the next ready ticket, claim it, verify its premises against primary sources, do the work, verify acceptance criteria, and close with evidence. The execution loop between tkt-orient (propose) and tkt-reconcile (wrap up). Use when working a ticket, picking up the next task, or asked 'work the frontier' / 'do the next ticket' / 'start on NN'. Trigger: work the frontier, do the next ticket, pick up work, claim and work, start ticket, next on the frontier, work a ticket, execute ticket, close ticket with evidence."

skills.name: to-questionnaire
skills.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

skills.name: to-spec
skills.description: "Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed."

skills.name: to-tickets
skills.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, created on the tkt tracker.

skills.name: triage
skills.description: "Move external requests (issues, PRs) and internal tkt tickets through triage roles: categorise, verify with real evidence, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs. Use when the user asks to triage issues or tickets, or when adopt-project seeds a board from raw items."

skills.name: verify-tkt-usage
skills.description: "Validate every tkt command this repo's skills reference against the live tkt capabilities manifest, catching drift when tkt renames, removes, or re-types a command or flag. Use after a tkt upgrade, or when auditing whether the skills still match the installed tkt."

skills.name: wait-what
skills.description: "Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it."

skills.name: wayfinder
skills.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on the issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

skills.name: wizard
skills.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

skills.description: "End-of-session closing bookend: groom the board, groom the environment, and land the cheap mechanical findings now. Runs reconcile-tickets then retro, then writes the guardrail/check/note or project-level skill that a recurring issue calls for instead of only filing it. Use when wrapping up a session, closing out, or asking 'let's wrap this up'."

catalog.name: adopt-project
catalog.description: Bring the grey-matter workflow into a repo that already has code and history: characterize the as-is model from the code, reconcile around what exists, seed a triaged board, and wire the plumbing — ending in a fully adopted repo. Use to adopt/onboard an existing (brownfield) project. Trigger: adopt this project, onboard existing repo, bring grey-matter into this codebase, brownfield adoption.
catalog.label: project:adopt-project

catalog.name: changelog
catalog.description: Maintain CHANGELOG.md in Keep a Changelog format with user-facing entries. Use when recording what changed for a release, updating the Unreleased section, or asked to write/update the changelog.
catalog.label: project:changelog

catalog.name: cheat-sheet
catalog.description: List every skill in this set by category with a one-line description. Use when the user wants a quick reference card of available skills, asks "what skills are there", or "list all commands".
catalog.label: project:cheat-sheet

catalog.name: code-review
catalog.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and files findings as tickets. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
catalog.label: project:code-review

catalog.name: codebase-design
catalog.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
catalog.label: project:codebase-design

catalog.name: compass
catalog.description: Find which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo. Use when you (or the agent) are unsure which skill to reach for, want to see how the skills fit together, or ask "what should I use for X".
catalog.label: project:compass

catalog.name: conformance-audit
catalog.description: Audit a repo's skills, tool scripts, agent guidance, and docs against grey-matter's current standards, then apply the mechanically-safe fixes behind an approval gate. Use to re-conform an adopted repo as guidance evolves, or as a step inside adopt-project. Trigger: conformance audit, check repo against standards, re-conform, does this repo still follow current conventions.
catalog.label: project:conformance-audit

catalog.name: curate-docs
catalog.description: Review docs/agents and .scratch for promotion and deletion: graduate mature notes into skills, move reference docs into a skill's references, and prune stale or superseded material.
catalog.label: project:curate-docs

catalog.name: delivery-dashboard
catalog.description: Maintain one evolving HTML dashboard showing what delivered work lets people do. Use when updating a delivery dashboard, showing shipped versus planned experiences, or presenting progress visually after work worth surfacing.
catalog.label: project:delivery-dashboard

catalog.name: diagnosing-bugs
catalog.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
catalog.label: project:diagnosing-bugs

catalog.name: domain-modeling
catalog.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model (app/backend/business software). Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording an ADR. For a game's real-time systems and design model, use game-modeling instead.
catalog.label: project:domain-modeling

catalog.name: foreign
catalog.description: Isolated user sentinel.
catalog.label: project:foreign

catalog.name: game-modeling
catalog.description: Build and sharpen a game's design model, mechanics, systems, and the core loop. Use when discussing game mechanics or terminology, writing a mechanics glossary, or recording a design decision. For a game's backend/economy/meta (business software), use domain-modeling instead.
catalog.label: project:game-modeling

catalog.name: game-native-design
catalog.description: Build games that feel like games, not web apps. Use when designing or reviewing game code: the loop, simulation state, performance, feel, or when another skill needs the game-native vocabulary. Reach for the matching engine appendix once the engine is known.
catalog.label: project:game-native-design

catalog.name: grill-me
catalog.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.
catalog.label: project:grill-me

catalog.name: grill-with-docs
catalog.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design that also leaves a paper trail (glossary and decision records). Use when grilling inside a working directory.
catalog.label: project:grill-with-docs

catalog.name: grilling
catalog.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
catalog.label: project:grilling

catalog.name: handoff
catalog.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.
catalog.label: project:handoff

catalog.name: implement
catalog.description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.
catalog.label: project:implement

catalog.name: implement-spec
catalog.description: Implement the result of to-spec and to-tickets in code, a whole spec on one integration branch.
catalog.label: project:implement-spec

catalog.name: improve-codebase-architecture
catalog.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, classify each by regime, present them as a full-bodied visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.
catalog.label: project:improve-codebase-architecture

catalog.name: init-project
catalog.description: Set up a new project's agent conventions once: AGENTS.md, scratch dir, gitignore, tkt, and whatever else the installed skills need tracked. Use when the user asks to initialize a repo for this workflow, or when adopt-project needs the missing plumbing created.
catalog.label: project:init-project

catalog.name: line-craft
catalog.description: Line craft for fiction prose and dialogue — feeling written as acts and errands, then the lines checked against a catalog of sentimental shapes. Use when drafting or revising story prose or dialogue, when the author rejects a line as sentimental, portentous or "emo", or when setting up a project's prose shape check.
catalog.label: project:line-craft

catalog.name: orient
catalog.description: Session-start pickup: get on the frontier and start the top ticket. Reads the board, resumes a live thread or claims the top ready ticket, and only pauses for something genuinely pressing. Use when starting or resuming a session, or asking 'where were we / what's next / pick up where we left off'.
catalog.label: project:orient

catalog.name: pr
catalog.description: Use when writing a PR body.
catalog.label: project:pr

catalog.name: prototype
catalog.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, explore what a UI should look like, or find whether a game mechanic is fun.
catalog.label: project:prototype

catalog.name: readme
catalog.description: Keep README.md honest and current: what the project is, how to install and use it, its status. Use at release time or when the README has drifted from reality.
catalog.label: project:readme

catalog.name: reconcile-tickets
catalog.description: End-of-session ticket pass: make every open ticket current, capture all untracked work as tickets, and set ordering so the frontier surfaces the right next picks. Use when wrapping up a session, auditing ticket health, or asking 'is everything captured?'.
catalog.label: project:reconcile-tickets

catalog.name: release
catalog.description: Prepare, verify, stage, publish or resume a coordinated versioned release with GitHub and plugin artifacts.
catalog.label: project:release

catalog.name: research
catalog.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a cited Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
catalog.label: project:research

catalog.name: research-audit
catalog.description: Validate and score a research findings file against its sources. Use after research produces a findings file, or when the user wants a cited analysis checked for citation accuracy, source trust, and currency.
catalog.label: project:research-audit

catalog.name: retro
catalog.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session: read it from a fresh context and propose environment fixes (checks, guardrails, steering), classified mechanical vs judgement. Use when a session ends, after a build that went sideways, or when wrap-session reaches its retro step.
catalog.label: project:retro

catalog.name: review-skill
catalog.description: Review one upstream skill for adaptation into grey-matter. Use when deciding whether to keep, adapt, drop, or replace a mattpocock/skills skill, one at a time.
catalog.label: project:review-skill

catalog.name: spike-options
catalog.description: Compare competing approaches with throwaway builds, then agree an integration plan. Use when a hard-to-reverse choice is cheap to spike and uncertainty needs observation rather than more reasoning: compare alternatives, spike options, test competing designs.
catalog.label: project:spike-options

catalog.name: sync
catalog.description: Pull grey-matter current and re-synchronize the coupled pieces — deployed skills, the tkt command surface, ticket IDs, and repo invariants — then redeploy. Use when updating this repo and pushing the skills back out to the harnesses, or asking to 'pull and deploy' / 'sync and redeploy'.
catalog.label: project:sync

catalog.name: tdd
catalog.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
catalog.label: project:tdd

catalog.name: teach
catalog.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.
catalog.label: project:teach

catalog.name: tkt-core
catalog.description: Track tasks as markdown files in your git repo. Use when managing tickets, checking the frontier (what's ready), claiming work, closing tasks, creating tickets, decomposing work into a task graph, or validating project health. Trigger: tkt, tickets, what to work on, create ticket, validate tickets, decompose, break into tasks, work breakdown, task graph, ticket format, blocked by, backlog, park this, defer.
catalog.label: project:tkt-core

catalog.name: tkt-orient
catalog.description: Start-of-session pickup from the reconciled plan and tickets: read the frontier, in-progress threads, and plan ordering that tkt-reconcile left behind, flag stale WIP, and propose the next step. Use when starting a session, resuming after a break, or asking 'where were we?' / 'what's next?' / 'pick up where we left off'. Trigger: start of session, orient, resume, pick up where we left off, where were we, what's next, catch me up, continue, session start, what's on the board.
catalog.label: project:tkt-orient

catalog.name: tkt-reconcile
catalog.description: End-of-session ticket + plan pass: make every ticket current, capture all open work as tickets, and re-prioritize/re-sequence the plan to match current priorities and work streams. Use when wrapping up a session, auditing ticket health, after planning, when work feels untracked, or asking 'is everything captured?' / 'update the plan'. Trigger: sync tickets, update the plan, re-prioritize, end of session ticket pass, ticket review, are tickets current, is everything tracked, ticket audit, ticket hygiene, wrap up tickets, tag scope, work stream.
catalog.label: project:tkt-reconcile

catalog.name: tkt-work
catalog.description: Claim and execute a ticket from the frontier: pick the next ready ticket, claim it, verify its premises against primary sources, do the work, verify acceptance criteria, and close with evidence. The execution loop between tkt-orient (propose) and tkt-reconcile (wrap up). Use when working a ticket, picking up the next task, or asked 'work the frontier' / 'do the next ticket' / 'start on NN'. Trigger: work the frontier, do the next ticket, pick up work, claim and work, start ticket, next on the frontier, work a ticket, execute ticket, close ticket with evidence.
catalog.label: project:tkt-work

catalog.name: to-questionnaire
catalog.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.
catalog.label: project:to-questionnaire

catalog.name: to-spec
catalog.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.
catalog.label: project:to-spec

catalog.name: to-tickets
catalog.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, created on the tkt tracker.
catalog.label: project:to-tickets

catalog.name: triage
catalog.description: Move external requests (issues, PRs) and internal tkt tickets through triage roles: categorise, verify with real evidence, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs. Use when the user asks to triage issues or tickets, or when adopt-project seeds a board from raw items.
catalog.label: project:triage

catalog.name: verify-tkt-usage
catalog.description: Validate every tkt command this repo's skills reference against the live tkt capabilities manifest, catching drift when tkt renames, removes, or re-types a command or flag. Use after a tkt upgrade, or when auditing whether the skills still match the installed tkt.
catalog.label: project:verify-tkt-usage

catalog.name: wait-what
catalog.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.
catalog.label: project:wait-what

catalog.name: wayfinder
catalog.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on the issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.
catalog.label: project:wayfinder

catalog.name: wizard
catalog.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.
catalog.label: project:wizard

catalog.name: wrap-session
catalog.description: End-of-session closing bookend: groom the board, groom the environment, and land the cheap mechanical findings now. Runs reconcile-tickets then retro, then writes the guardrail/check/note or project-level skill that a recurring issue calls for instead of only filing it. Use when wrapping up a session, closing out, or asking 'let's wrap this up'.
catalog.label: project:wrap-session

catalog.name: writing-for-agents
catalog.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
catalog.label: project:writing-for-agents

grey-matter:pr	Use when writing a PR body.
grey-matter:prototype	Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, explore what a UI should look like, or find whether a game mechanic is fun.
grey-matter:readme	Keep README.md honest and current: what the project is, how to install and use it, its status. Use at release time or when the README has drifted from reality.
grey-matter:reconcile-tickets	End-of-session ticket pass: make every open ticket current, capture all untracked work as tickets, and set ordering so the frontier surfaces the right next picks. Use when wrapping up a session, auditing ticket health, or asking 'is everything captured?'.
grey-matter:release	Prepare, verify, stage, publish or resume a coordinated versioned release with GitHub and plugin artifacts.
grey-matter:research	Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a cited Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
grey-matter:research-audit	Validate and score a research findings file against its sources. Use after research produces a findings file, or when the user wants a cited analysis checked for citation accuracy, source trust, and currency.
grey-matter:retro	Conduct a retrospective on a coding session: read it from a fresh context and propose environment fixes (checks, guardrails, steering), classified mechanical vs judgement. Use when a session ends, after a build that went sideways, or when wrap-session reaches its retro step.
grey-matter:review-skill	Review one upstream skill for adaptation into grey-matter. Use when deciding whether to keep, adapt, drop, or replace a mattpocock/skills skill, one at a time.
grey-matter:spike-options	Compare competing approaches with throwaway builds, then agree an integration plan. Use when a hard-to-reverse choice is cheap to spike and uncertainty needs observation rather than more reasoning: compare alternatives, spike options, test competing designs.
grey-matter:sync	Pull grey-matter current and re-synchronize the coupled pieces — deployed skills, the tkt command surface, ticket IDs, and repo invariants — then redeploy. grey-matter:tdd	Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
grey-matter:teach	Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.
grey-matter:to-questionnaire	Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.
grey-matter:to-spec	Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.
grey-matter:to-tickets	Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, created on the tkt tracker.
grey-matter:triage	Move external requests (issues, PRs) and internal tkt tickets through triage roles: categorise, verify with real evidence, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs. Use when the user asks to triage issues or tickets, or when adopt-project seeds a board from raw items.
grey-matter:verify-tkt-usage	Validate every tkt command this repo's skills reference against the live tkt capabilities manifest, catching drift when tkt renames, removes, or re-types a command or flag. Use after a tkt upgrade, or when auditing whether the skills still match the installed tkt.
grey-matter:wait-what	Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.
grey-matter:wayfinder	Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on the issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.
grey-matter:wizard	Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. grey-matter:wrap-session	End-of-session closing bookend: groom the board, groom the environment, and land the cheap mechanical findings now. grey-matter:release	Prepare, verify, stage, publish or resume a coordinated versioned release with GitHub and plugin artifacts.
grey-matter:research	Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a cited Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
grey-matter:research-audit	Validate and score a research findings file against its sources. Use after research produces a findings file, or when the user wants a cited analysis checked for citation accuracy, source trust, and currency.
grey-matter:retro	Conduct a retrospective on a coding session: read it from a fresh context and propose environment fixes (checks, guardrails, steering), classified mechanical vs judgement. Use when a session ends, after a build that went sideways, or when wrap-session reaches its retro step.
grey-matter:review-skill	Review one upstream skill for adaptation into grey-matter. Use when deciding whether to keep, adapt, drop, or replace a mattpocock/skills skill, one at a time.
grey-matter:spike-options	Compare competing approaches with throwaway builds, then agree an integration plan. Use when a hard-to-reverse choice is cheap to spike and uncertainty needs observation rather than more reasoning: compare alternatives, spike options, test competing designs.
grey-matter:sync	Pull grey-matter current and re-synchronize the coupled pieces — deployed skills, the tkt command surface, ticket IDs, and repo invariants — then redeploy. Use when updating this repo and pushing the skills back out to the harnesses, or asking to 'pull and deploy' / 'sync and redeploy'.
grey-matter:tdd	Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
grey-matter:teach	Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.
grey-matter:to-questionnaire	Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.
grey-matter:to-spec	Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.
grey-matter:to-tickets	Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, created on the tkt tracker.
grey-matter:triage	Move external requests (issues, PRs) and internal tkt tickets through triage roles: categorise, verify with real evidence, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs. Use when the user asks to triage issues or tickets, or when adopt-project seeds a board from raw items.
grey-matter:verify-tkt-usage	Validate every tkt command this repo's skills reference against the live tkt capabilities manifest, catching drift when tkt renames, removes, or re-types a command or flag. Use after a tkt upgrade, or when auditing whether the skills still match the installed tkt.
grey-matter:wait-what	Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.
grey-matter:wayfinder	Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on the issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.
grey-matter:wizard	Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.
grey-matter:wrap-session	End-of-session closing bookend: groom the board, groom the environment, and land the cheap mechanical findings now. Runs reconcile-tickets then retro, then writes the guardrail/check/note or project-level skill that a recurring issue calls for instead of only filing it. Use when wrapping up a session, closing out, or asking 'let's wrap this up'.
grey-matter:writing-for-agents	Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
migrate-workflows	Automatically migrate legacy workflows to modern skills across global and workspace configurations. Scans for existing workflows, creates target SKILL.md files, and safely archives old workflow files.
run-workflow	How to write and run a dynamic workflow script with the `run_workflow` tool: a Python script that orchestrates many agents with `agent`, `parallel`, `pipeline`, and `phase`. Use when a task splits into many independent or staged pieces of agent work (fan out over files, modules, bugs, or review angles, then aggregate), or when the user asks for a workflow. Don't use for a single delegated task (use a subagent) or for legacy workflow files (see migrate-workflows).

research.text:
---
topic: Windows Codex and Claude Code direct binaries
date: 2026-10-24
status: complete
confidence: verified-metadata
---

# Summary

The pinned versions both publish native x64 and ARM64 Windows executables. Codex also publishes a complete package archive with companion tools; prefer that archive for a portable tool directory. Claude publishes a single executable. No installers or executables were run; no model calls were made.

# Findings

## Codex 0.147.0

[L1:verified] Release API metadata: https://api.github.com/repos/openai/codex/releases/tags/rust-v0.147.0 . SHA256 below comes from GitHub asset digest metadata, except the x64 package was also downloaded and locally hashed.

| Asset | Bytes | SHA256 | URL |
|---|---:|---|---|
| codex-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.exe | 250102064 | `1f0e8c2dd3c6b471e985fac76908366c1cf31155094fde606fb2d3052cf00584` | [download](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/download/rust-v0.147.0/codex-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.exe) |
| codex-package-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.gz | 117548230 | `4533928d72ac4d7c19f16e8c4acdfd02dc255d2aeeb2f6d7dfd45493ec4c0806` | [download](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/download/rust-v0.147.0/codex-package-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.gz) |
| codex-package-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.gz | 126777040 | `c156c8feb8cb20197bf74d2c6daffed1fec0a8c21a03bc2ca90d7ff81927b0c5` | [download](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/download/rust-v0.147.0/codex-package-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.gz) |
| codex-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe | 298668336 | `935a1911ed2556e4ffcec995f4886ac2ac425863ba26fed264df62e30272ad9d` | [download](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/download/rust-v0.147.0/codex-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe) |

[L1:verified] Actual x64 tar members (`tar -tzf /tmp/codex-windows-package.tar.gz`):

```text
bin
bin/codex-code-mode-host.exe
bin/codex.exe
codex-package.json
codex-path
codex-path/rg.exe
codex-resources
codex-resources/codex-command-runner.exe
codex-resources/codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe
```

Evidence: `shasum -a 256 /tmp/codex-windows-package.tar.gz` → `c156c8feb8cb20197bf74d2c6daffed1fec0a8c21a03bc2ca90d7ff81927b0c5`, matching GitHub metadata.

[L1:verified] Version-pinned layout source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/scripts/codex_package/layout.py . Keep the entire archive layout and call `bin/codex.exe` by absolute path. A single executable download omits the packaged code-mode host, ripgrep and Windows sandbox companion executables. ARM64 archive members were not downloaded/observed; the common layout source defines the same Windows names.

[L4:reported] Set process-local `CODEX_HOME` to a dedicated state directory before launching, and use file credential storage if avoiding shared OS credential storage is required. `CODEX_HOME` alone is not a security isolation boundary: system/project configuration and the OS credential store may still apply. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-advanced .

## Claude Code 2.1.310

[L1:verified] Official installer https://claude.ai/install.ps1 sets its download base to `https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases`, reads a manifest, verifies SHA256, then runs `claude install`. To retain portable placement, download the pinned executable directly and do not invoke `install`. The script fetches latest for bootstrap even when given a specific install target.

Manifest: https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/2.1.310/manifest.json

| Platform | Bytes | SHA256 | URL |
|---|---:|---|---|
| win32-x64 | 296791712 | `f9a3920634ae3b961ee92c2eb58d0051f5f8852b120983d0a4f57b6a5efeba61` | [claude.exe](https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/2.1.310/win32-x64/claude.exe) |
| win32-arm64 | 280850592 | `91da8a2247a8806162319bcdf3e70c6ffeeb58b568481a9827fbff167a694edb` | [claude.exe](https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/2.1.310/win32-arm64/claude.exe) |

These downloads are executables, not archives; there are no archive members. Binary bytes were not downloaded or hashed locally.

[L4:reported] Official integrity guidance publishes a detached manifest signature and Windows Authenticode signature. Signature URL: https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/2.1.310/manifest.json.sig ; public key: https://downloads.claude.ai/keys/claude-code.asc . Expected documented fingerprint: `31DD DE24 DDFA B679 F42D 7BD2 BAA9 29FF 1A7E CACE`. Verify the manifest signature, binary SHA256, and `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` before execution. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#binary-integrity-and-code-signing . Signature verification was not performed in this research.

[L4:reported] Set process-local `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to a dedicated directory for settings, history and plugins. Set `DISABLE_UPDATES=1` for pinned distribution (blocks manual and automatic updates); `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` only blocks the background updater. Do not change global PATH or run the installer for a portable launcher. Native Windows currently supports PowerShell without Git for Windows; Git Bash is optional but required for the Bash and Monitor tools. Native Windows sandboxing is unsupported. Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup .

# Sources

All cited sources are official vendor metadata, code or documentation. Version-pinned metadata is stronger evidence for exact download hashes than moving setup documentation.

# Related Topics

Windows portable verification launchers; architecture detection; state isolation.

# Related Tools

PowerShell `Get-FileHash`, `Get-AuthenticodeSignature`; `tar`; GPG.

# Open Questions

Windows runtime smoke tests remain necessary. No executable was run, and neither vendor documents these state-directory settings as complete hermetic isolation from managed policy, project files, inherited environment or machine credentials.

[L1:inferred] Invoke an absolute path to the pinned executable, verify version before and after validation, and hash downloaded bytes with `Get-FileHash`. research.text:
---
topic: Codex 0.147.0 Windows user-skill isolation
date: 2026-10-24
status: complete
confidence: verified-source
---

# Summary

Codex 0.147.0 has no user-skill-root replacement setting in its pinned skill configuration schema or host root resolver. On Windows, changing HOME, USERPROFILE and CODEX_HOME does not redirect the additional user skill root: the resolver uses the Windows known-folder Profile path through `dirs::home_dir()`. `skills.config` can disable individual discovered skills by exact path or name; it cannot prevent root discovery or exclude a directory tree.

# Findings

## Exact root behavior

[L1:verified] [Pinned host root resolver](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_roots.rs#L29-L45) calls `dirs::home_dir()` directly. In [lines 110–129](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_roots.rs#L110-L129), each User configuration layer adds all of:

- `<user-config-folder>/skills` (the deprecated CODEX_HOME-based root).
- `<dirs::home_dir()>/.agents/skills`.
- The system skill cache beneath the user config folder.

The function has no environment-variable branch or parameter sourced from an override for the home root. Plugin and extra skill roots are additive (`roots.extend`), not replacements ([lines 57–83](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_roots.rs#L57-L83)).

[L1:verified] [Pinned Cargo.lock](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/Cargo.lock) pins `dirs 6.0.0`, `dirs-sys 0.5.0`. Exact published crate bytes were downloaded from [dirs 6.0.0](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/dirs/6.0.0/download) and [dirs-sys 0.5.0](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/dirs-sys/0.5.0/download), then read with tar without installation. `dirs-6.0.0/src/win.rs` defines `home_dir()` as `dirs_sys::known_folder_profile()`. `dirs-sys-0.5.0/src/lib.rs` defines that as `known_folder(Shell::FOLDERID_Profile)`, which calls `SHGetKnownFolderPath(&folder_id, 0, null_mut(), &mut path_ptr)`. Neither function reads HOME or USERPROFILE.

[L1:inferred] Therefore a same-user process with overridden environment variables still resolves the real Windows profile known folder. This is independent of working directory; an outside-home temporary directory alone should not remove this User-scoped root.

## Ancestor traversal hypothesis

[L1:verified] [Pinned ancestor root logic](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_roots.rs#L168-L292) searches ancestors for project root markers, then discovers `.agents/skills` only between that root and cwd. If no marker is found, `find_project_root` returns cwd (line 271), so only cwd is checked for repository skills. Setting `project_root_markers=[]` likewise returns cwd immediately. It does not remove the independent User root above. Moving TEMP outside the user profile remains a useful discriminating test, but is not a source-supported fix for User-scoped discovery.

## Configuration limits

[L1:verified] [Pinned SkillsConfig](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/config/src/skills_config.rs#L12-L35) contains `bundled`, `include_instructions`, and `config`. Entries contain optional `path` or `name`, plus `enabled`. No root override or root exclusion exists there.

[L1:verified] [Config rule parsing](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/core-skills/src/config_rules.rs#L12-L76) only consumes User and SessionFlags layers. A path rule canonicalizes its supplied path; a name rule is an exact string selector. [Policy application](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/skills/src/policy.rs#L12-L44) inserts the exact path in a disabled set; names match `skill.name == name`. There is no prefix/tree/glob matching. The [host service](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_service.rs#L288-L345) applies disabled paths after loading skill outcomes. Disabled entries therefore still require discovery; they are not filesystem isolation.

[L1:verified] `bundled_skills_enabled=false` only retains roots whose scope is not System; it does not remove User roots ([host service lines 164–183](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.147.0/codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_service.rs#L164-L183)). `skills.include_instructions=false` controls prompt injection, not discovery, per its schema comment.

# Sources

All links above are pinned official Codex source or exact published dependency crates. Local inspected copies are under `/tmp/codex-isolation`; dependency archives are `/tmp/dirs.crate` and `/tmp/dirs-sys.crate`.

# Related Topics

Disposable Windows user/VM boundaries; skill discovery versus skill enablement.

# Related Tools

Codex app-server `skills/list`; Windows known-folder API; Rust dirs crate.

# Open Questions

No supported CLI/environment setting that replaces or suppresses this home root was found in the pinned resolver/schema/service path. A separate Windows account or disposable VM provides a different known-folder Profile without modifying the existing user's directories; actual harness provisioning remains outside this source audit. No user directory was changed and no model call was made.

# Kiro CLI 2.34.0 Windows isolation override

Exact supported variable: **`KIRO_HOME`**. It names the replacement `.kiro` directory itself, not a parent home directory. No `KIRO_CLI_HOME` or `Q_*` override is needed or established by this research.

[L4:verified] [Official CLI commands reference](https://kiro.dev/docs/reference/cli-commands/) documents `KIRO_HOME` as the global Kiro directory override covering MCP configuration/sign-ins, permissions, sessions, Powers, settings, custom agents, Skills, Steering, Workflows, and V3 state. [Official settings reference](https://kiro.dev/docs/reference/settings/) independently lists global agents, prompts, skills, steering, settings, and sessions, with independent profiles as its use case. Both pages were read on 2026-10-24.

[L3:verified] [Official 2.3.0 changelog](https://kiro.dev/changelog/cli/2-3/) introduces `KIRO_HOME` and explicitly directs setting it before launch. [Official 2.31.0 changelog](https://kiro.dev/changelog/cli/2-31/) says support was extended across V3 configuration and state. Therefore documented support precedes pinned 2.34.0.

Use in the environment of the actual ACP child process:

```powershell
$env:KIRO_HOME = 'C:\path\to\fixture\kiro-state'
& 'C:\path\to\pinned\kiro-cli.exe' acp
```

For a programmatic launcher, insert `KIRO_HOME` into the environment passed to `CreateProcess`/subprocess launch. Do not depend on shell HOME or USERPROFILE redirects. Ensure an already-running Kiro engine cannot be reused from a prior process with another environment.

[L1:inferred] Re-run the same ACP metadata-only check after setting this variable, and require both real-user skill absence and fixture skill presence as the pass signal. This research did not execute Windows Kiro and cannot claim observed native isolation. If user skill paths remain, stop: documented override behavior and observed behavior disagree; do not label the launch isolated or guess another variable.

Workspace `.kiro` files are a separate configuration scope; run from the intended fixture directory. An explicitly configured resource containing an absolute real-user path can still reference it even when global state moves. `KIRO_HOME` relocates application state; it is not an OS filesystem sandbox.

Evidence: official docs and 2.3.0/2.31.0 release notes read through web tool → exact variable, directory semantics, and pre-2.34.0 V3 support confirmed. No installs, model calls, or native executable probes performed.
